# bytebase_iam_policy (Resource)

The IAM policy resource.

## Keyed Bindings

Use `bindings` (provider 3.25.1 or later) for focused member and condition
diffs. Keys are chosen by you and remain stable when a binding's members or
condition changes. For an existing policy, follow the
[3.25.1 migration guide](https://github.com/bytebase/terraform-provider-bytebase/blob/main/migration/3.25.1.md).

```hcl
resource "bytebase_iam_policy" "project" {
  parent = bytebase_project.payments.name

  bindings = {
    readers = {
      role = "roles/sqlEditorReadUser"
      members = [
        "group:team-a@example.com",
        "group:team-b@example.com",
      ]
      condition = {
        database         = "instances/prod/databases/payments"
        expire_timestamp = "2027-12-31T00:00:00Z"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

This resource owns the **entire** policy, not just the bindings or members
listed in the configuration. Grants added outside Terraform appear as drift
and are removed by the next apply unless added to the configuration. Use one
IAM policy resource per parent, and retain any grants needed by the account
running Terraform. Bytebase may reject an empty policy; an empty map is not
a way to bypass the server's policy safeguards.

Each map entry must have a unique role and condition. Use one entry with all
members rather than two entries with the same role and condition. Duplicate
bindings returned by the server are read as one binding containing their
combined members, so additional grants are not hidden.

Keyed policies support the structured condition fields listed below. Other
CEL expressions or condition metadata produce an error rather than being
silently rewritten with weaker restrictions.

Keys are not stored by Bytebase. Refresh preserves them by matching role and
condition. Imported policies and unmatched remote bindings receive generated
keys of the form `roles/role#<hash>`. Use those keys in the configuration or
rename them explicitly; a rename changes the map diff, not the resource ID.

When the server supplies a policy etag, updates of the same parent send the
version retained by refresh. A concurrent change after the plan makes apply
fail rather than overwrite the newer policy. Review the latest policy and
create a new plan; the provider does not automatically retry a stale policy
write. State created before etags were tracked must be refreshed before
updating. Initial writes and parent changes read the target policy immediately
before writing, so changes before that read are not protected by the plan.
A server returning no etag (including a policy not yet stored) cannot provide
version-based conflict protection.

## Legacy Configuration

Existing `iam_policy { binding {} }` configurations and state remain
supported, with their existing whole-binding diffs. To migrate, replace that
block with `bindings`, choose stable keys, and copy every role, member, and
condition. Use `condition = { ... }` rather than a `condition { ... }` block.
Do not configure both forms. Review the plan before applying: changing input
forms does not replace the resource or perform separate revoke/grant calls.

In the keyed form, omitted `environment_ids` means no environment restriction,
while `environment_ids = []` denies DDL/DML in every environment. Legacy
condition blocks materialize an omitted environment set as empty. When
migrating a conditional grant, preserve an existing `resource.environment_id
in []` restriction with an explicit `environment_ids = []`; inspect the
stored policy and do not remove that restriction unintentionally.

This provider uses plugin protocol v6 with an SDK compatibility layer,
requiring Terraform 1.1.5 or later.
Features using write-only attributes require Terraform 1.11 or later.

## Schema

### Optional

- `bindings` (Map of Object) Bindings keyed by a stable, user-chosen name. Cannot be used with `iam_policy`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bindings))
- `iam_policy` (Block List, Max: 1) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--iam_policy))
- `parent` (String) The IAM policy parent name for the policy, support "projects/{resource id}" or "workspaces/{workspace id}". Defaults to the workspace if not specified.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `etag` (String) The server policy version used to detect concurrent writes.

<a id="nestedatt--bindings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bindings`

Required:

- `role` (String) The role full name in `roles/{id}` format.
- `members` (Set of String) Members in the same formats supported by legacy bindings below. Must not be empty.

Optional:

- `condition` (Object) The same fields as the legacy condition below: `database`, `schema`, `tables`, `expire_timestamp`, and `environment_ids`.

<a id="nestedblock--iam_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `iam_policy`

Optional:

- `binding` (Block Set) The binding in the IAM policy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--iam_policy--binding))

<a id="nestedblock--iam_policy--binding"></a>
### Nested Schema for `iam_policy.binding`

Optional:

- `condition` (Block Set) Match the condition limit. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--iam_policy--binding--condition))
- `members` (Set of String) A set of memebers. The value can be "allUsers", "user:{email}", "group:{email}", "serviceAccount:{email}" or "workloadIdentity:{email}".
- `role` (String) The role full name in roles/{id} format.

<a id="nestedblock--iam_policy--binding--condition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `iam_policy.binding.condition`

Optional:

- `database` (String) The accessible database full name in instances/{instance resource id}/databases/{database name} format. Only works for the role with bb.sql.x permissions.
- `environment_ids` (Set of String) The environment ID list to allow the DDL/DML operation in the SQL Editor. Only works for the role with bb.sql.ddl or bb.sql.dml permissions.
- `expire_timestamp` (String) The expiration timestamp in YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ format
- `schema` (String) The accessible schema in the database. Must configure with the database.
- `tables` (Set of String) The accessible table list. Must configure with the database.
